name: Netlist Connectivity & Topology Analyzer
description: Graph-theoretic analysis of a board's netlist: electrical islands, single points of failure, high-fanout signals, missing decoupling and topology metrics.
description_full: Models the netlist as a graph and applies graph algorithms to answer global questions that DRC and ERC do not ask. Reports disconnected electrical islands, floating and single-pad nets, unrouted nets, high-fanout signal nets, ICs without local decoupling on their own rail-and-ground pair, articulation points and bridges in the signal topology, and betweenness-centrality hub ranking. Results appear in a tabbed dialog with cross-probing to the PCB editor, and export to self-contained HTML, JSON and SVG. A head-less command-line runner allows the same analysis in CI. Power and ground nets are deliberately excluded from the topology projection: rails touch nearly every part, so including them makes the component graph almost complete and destroys all structural information.
